To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
dopamine receptor agonist-induced decreases in STN neuronal activity are not associated with selective stimulation of striatal dopamine D1 and D 2 receptors.
the activity of the subthalamic (STN) neurons is increased in the dopamine-depleted state, and that the activity of STN neurons can be reduced by dopamine receptor agonists.
dopamine agonists reduced the activity of the subthalamic neurons of rats with lesions of the nigrosriatal pathway, but increased the activity of subthalamic neurons in intact rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapies for Parkinson's disease (PD).
the role of the basal ganglia in the pathophysiology and treatment of movement disorders.
the role that the subthalamic (STN) nucleus plays in the pathophysiology and treatment of Parkinson's disease (PD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the STN is not the primary source of the abnormal movement in Parkinson’s disease.
the STN is a critical component of the pathophysiology underlying Parkinson's disease, and the response of the STN is critical for the therapeutic efficacy of dopamine agonists.
dopamine receptor agonist drugs do not act directly on subthalamic nucleus cells to decrease activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the STN in a rodent model of Parkinson’s Disease is tonically overactive, and that dopamine receptor agonist stimulation reduces the overactivity of the STN.
the STN is not a simple relay station for the transmission of information from the striatum, and that dopamine receptor agonist therapy may have complex effects on the activity of this nucleus.
D1 receptors have a tonic inhibitory influence on STN neuronal activity and that D2 receptors have a tonic excitatory influence on STN neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the subthalamic region is a critical component of the basal ganglia, and that its activity is modulated by dopamine.
dopamine receptor stimulation can have a biphasic effect on subthalamic nucleus neurons.
the STN is not just a relay station for information from the cortex, but it has an important role in motor control.
